note: 1st daughter; *** a twin of William John *** *** NOW ON A DOCUMENT RATHER THAN A TREE'S SILENCE, 14 September 2026: THE 1911 CENSUS ENTERS HER AS "SINGLE", AGED 41, in her married sister ISABELLA DALLING'S house at Northam, as "Sister". *** This archive recorded her with no husband because a tree gave her none, which is evidence of nothing. Now it is evidence. Whether she married AFTER 1911 is untested - she lived until 1940. *** A FIND A GRAVE entry for a Kathleen Georgina Taylor at BROMPTON CEMETERY, London, died 24 JULY 1942, was seen and NOT attached: *** this woman died 29 February 1940, two years earlier and in a different place. *** AND SHE IS A TWIN - settled 14 September 2026. *** The 1871 census has her and WILLIAM JOHN both as infants in the house on 2 April 1871, and their parents' banns were called at Bideford on 9 JANUARY 1870. Two children of one mother, both alive in a house fifteen months after the banns, cannot be separate births. *** So the family had TWO sets of twins: this pair in 1870 and Irene's in 1879. *** *** AND THE 1921 CENSUS ANSWERS HER, NOT WITH A DATE BUT WITH A LIFE. *** At FIFTY she is still in her sister Isabella's house at FORE STREET, NORTHAM - and the occupation column reads *** "HOME INVALID". *** The eldest daughter of ten, unmarried at fifty, an invalid in her younger sister's home, with her brother-in-law the insurance agent and three children about her. She died in 1940, aged sixty-nine. *** Nothing here had suggested it, because a tree records marriages and not infirmity. *** AND THE INDEX CALLS HER "KATHLEEN GEORGINA DALLING" - the enumerator wrote the household's surname against every line. That is the same trap that cost this archive a retraction over the 1895 Buenos Aires census, in English, twenty-six years later. *** AND THE 1939 REGISTER, eighteen years after the last, at 26 FORE STREET, NORTHAM. *** Born *** 4 NOVEMBER 1870 *** - this archive's date confirmed to the day, and with it the reading that she and WILLIAM JOHN were twins. Occupation: *** "INCAPACITATED". *** She died five months later, on 29 February 1940. *** THREE RECORDS, TWENTY-EIGHT YEARS, ONE HOUSE: *** single at 41 in 1911, "home invalid" at 50 in 1921, "incapacitated" at 68 in 1939 - always in her sister Isabella's household. The eldest of ten, and the only one who never left. *** This archive read her blank husband column as a question about marriage. It was never a question about marriage. *** And the Register's own marital status column against her is left EMPTY, where the others read Married and Single - recorded as blank, not read as single.
source: England and Wales Census 1911, Northam, RG14 piece/folio 299, ED 6, schedule 150 - index read 14 Sep 2026; and the England and Wales censuses of 1871, 1901 and 1911 - indexes read 14 Sep 2026; and the 1921 Census of England & Wales - RG15, read 14 Sep 2026; and the 1939 Register, RG101/6826D/008/16 - read 14 Sep 2026

note: Children: William Archibald (1893), Gladys Helen (Jun 1900). Same birth month as Kathleen - twins, or one date is wrong. *** HIS MARRIAGE IS NOT FOUND, and the tree's "Fanny Ellen Jefferey" is NOT CONFIRMED - searched 14 September 2026. *** No marriage of a Fanny Jefferey to a William John Taylor surfaces anywhere, while the same search method named five of his sisters' husbands in ten minutes. Devon holds other William John Taylors marrying in the right window - to MARY CONIBEER in 1904 and to MARGARET SCOTT WALKINSHAW in 1897 - and NONE is shown to be this man. *** Left open rather than guessed at. *** *** THE CENSUSES ANSWER MOST OF IT, 14 September 2026. *** 1901 at Northam: "spouse FANNY HELEN TAYLOR, children GLADYS HELEN and WILLIAM ARCHIBALD". 1911 at *** PAIGNTON *** in SOUTH Devon: "married 1892". *** So he married in 1892 to a FANNY HELEN - and the tree's surname JEFFEREY is supported by no record anywhere. *** The only Fanny Jeffreys to marry a Taylor in England married a JAMES WILLIAM Taylor at Dukinfield, CHESHIRE, in 1893: a likely tree conflation, said as a suspicion and not as a finding. *** AND HE IS A TWIN OF KATHLEEN GEORGINA *** - see her row. *** His move to PAIGNTON matters beyond him: his sister LUCY ELIZABETH had her banns called at CHURSTON FERRERS, three miles away, in 1909. The brother was there first, and she followed him eighty miles from Northam. ***
source: MyHeritage tree; searched against the Devon parish registers 14 Sep 2026 without result; and the England and Wales censuses of 1871, 1901 and 1911 - indexes read 14 Sep 2026

note: 4th daughter; a twin *** HER HUSBAND IS NAMED AND HER MARRIAGE DATED: HENRY ALBERT BURTON, at NORTHAM on 30 AUGUST 1900. *** Recorded here as "m. Burton" until 14 September 2026. *** The first of two sisters to marry at Northam within a fortnight, four months after their mother died. *** *** AND THE CENSUSES TRACE A JOURNEY NOBODY HERE HAD SEEN. *** She married at Northam on 30 August 1900 and was living in BERMONDSEY, SOUTH LONDON at the census of 31 March 1901 - seven months later. By 1911 the Burtons are back at BIDEFORD, four miles from where she was born, with two sons: CHARLES WILLIAM BURTON and ALBERT EDWARD BURTON. She died in Devon in 1969. *** AND IN 1921 THE BURTONS ARE AT 5 KINGSLEY TERRACE, BIDEFORD. *** Henry Albert Burton, 45, is an *** ASSURANCE AGENT for the PRUDENTIAL *** - so both he and his brother-in-law Henry Dalling sold insurance. Their son CHARLES WILLIAM is 13; *** ALBERT EDWARD, in the house in 1911, is not there. *** They keep two boarders. *** AND THE RETURN GIVES IRENE'S BIRTHPLACE AS BERMONDSEY, WHICH IS WRONG: *** she was born at Northam and her own marriage act says so. Her husband was born at Bermondsey, he filled the form, and he carried his own answer across to her line. A census birthplace is only as good as the person holding the pen.
